messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure in the test `testGetLineNumberWithCR()` is related to how the line number is tracked in the CSVParser when the line separator is the carriage return (CR, '\r'). The test uses a CSVParser constructed with input containing only CR as line separators and expects the line number to be 1 at the start.

The chain of calls for getting the line number in CSVParser goes to `lexer.getLineNumber()`, which in turn calls `ExtendedBufferedReader.getLineNumber()`. The line number is managed by `ExtendedBufferedReader` via a `lineCounter` field.

Inspecting the `ExtendedBufferedReader` class shows that its `read()` method increments the line counter only when it encounters a newline character (`'\n'`). Its `readLine()` method relies on the superclass `BufferedReader.readLine()` and increments the line counter whenever a line is read, regardless of the specific line separator, because `BufferedReader.readLine()` normalizes line endings treating CR, LF, and CRLF uniformly.

The problem arises because the test uses `CSVFormat` with a line separator of `'\r'` (CR), but the `read()` method only increments line count on `'\n'`. This inconsistency means line numbers will not be incremented correctly when CR is the line separator in some cases.

Specifically, since `read()` increments lines only for LF but not CR, but `readLine()` increments for every line regardless, and since the parser uses read lines differently, this leads to inconsistent line number tracking. The current implementation does not increment line count on CR alone in `read()`, which causes the reported line numbers to be incorrect when CR is the separator.

The current bug report highlights this inconsistency in `ExtendedBufferedReader`: it handles `'\n'` endings for line count in `read()` but relies on `BufferedReader.readLine()` for normalization in `readLine()`, which handles CR, LF and CRLF correctly. To fix this, `ExtendedBufferedReader` should also increment the line counter on CR characters in `read()` and ensure consistent handling for all line separator types, including CR alone.

The test failure is thus caused by `ExtendedBufferedReader.read()` not incrementing `lineCounter` for `'\r'` line separators, leading to the CSVParser returning wrong line numbers for inputs with CR line separators.

Recent bug reports do not appear directly relevant to this root cause, except the current bug report describing the inconsistent EOL handling in `ExtendedBufferedReader`.

Summary:
- `testGetLineNumberWithCR()` fails due to incorrect line number counting with CR line separators.
- `ExtendedBufferedReader.read()` only increments lineCounter on LF (`'\n'`), not CR (`'\r'`).
- `ExtendedBufferedReader.readLine()` calls `BufferedReader.readLine()` which normalizes CR and increments lineCounter each read.
- This mismatch causes inconsistent line counting depending on reading method used.
- Fix requires updating `ExtendedBufferedReader.read()` to increment lineCounter for CR (`'\r'`) as well.

This explains the cause of the test failure based on provided code snippets and bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
